title: 8. Stage 2 Technical Structure, Institutional Flow & Momentum Setup

epigraph.quote: The tape is not always right about value, but it is almost always right about timing. A great business in a broken chart is a great business you can buy cheaper later.
epigraph.author: Stan Weinstein, Secrets for Profiting in Bull and Bear Markets (1988), applied to Netweb on 23–25 November 2026

web_blocks.html: Every price and chart level here is labeled by source date. The verified NSE ledger cutoff is 23 November 2026 (close ₹4,010.60). The live TradingView snapshot ran on 25 November 2026 (close ₹4,010.80). Both feeds show clear chart damage since our 12 November review (close ₹4,151.90, just 0.65% below the 200-day SMA). By 25 November, Netweb broke cleanly below its 200-day SMA (₹4,217.26, now -4.90%). It sits 9.69% below its 50-day SMA (₹4,440.99), 11.99% below its 30-week SMA (₹4,556.98), and 6.64% below its 10-week EMA (₹4,296.24). The classifier is clear: Stage 4, AVOID_STAGE4_OR_BROKEN, CAP_REJECTED, and absent from TheWrap Stage 2 list.

web_blocks.takeaway: Every major trend filter is broken. Since 12 November, Netweb lost its 200-day SMA (-4.90%), lost its 4-hour bounce turn, logged 8 distribution days in 25 sessions, and printed -30.61% 63-day relative strength vs Nifty 50.

web_blocks.html: Our 25 November 2026 multi-timeframe scan shows no short-term bounce window either. On 12 November, 4-hour RSI (49.37) topped daily RSI (43.85) as price reclaimed its 4-hour EMA20. That turn has now failed. Today, 4-hour RSI is 42.50, daily RSI is 40.96 (39.96 on the 23 Nov NSE ledger), and weekly RSI is 43.49. Price (₹4,010.80) sits below both 4-hour EMA20 (₹4,078.19) and 4-hour SMA50 (₹4,177.81). Netweb is also outside NSE F&O (`NOT_OPTIONABLE_OR_ILLIQUID`). With no listed options chain, all risk control must happen in cash equity.

We reconcile our two automated stage tags plainly. The 23 November NSE ledger tags Netweb as Stage 1 (Basing) because price held above its ₹3,716.10 63-day low. Yet the 25 November TradingView classifier reads Stage 4 (`AVOID_STAGE4_OR_BROKEN`, `CAP_REJECTED`). Price sits 11.99% below its 30-week SMA (₹4,556.98), 9.69% below a falling 50-day SMA (₹4,440.99), and 4.90% below its 200-day SMA (₹4,217.26). We enforce the stricter Stage 4 tag. A real Stage 1 base needs a flat 30-week line and fading selling, not 8 distribution days and -33.16% 28-day relative strength.

Shareholding flow backs up the weak chart. Promoter ownership fell from 75.45% at listing to 64.16% by September 2026. That drop reflects not just IPO and QIP dilution, but a 3.65% (>₹514 crore) block sale of 20.79 lakh shares by four promoters on 12 February 2026. FII ownership slipped from over 12% in late 2024 to 9.47% in September 2026, while retail holders rose past 2.6 lakh. August 2026 QIP funds who paid ₹4,790 sit 16.3% underwater, and the promoter lock-up ends in February 2027. Dry volume (0.51x–0.64x) and 8 distribution days confirm zero fund buying.

Market context sharpens the cost of waiting. On the 23 November NSE ledger, Nifty 50 is in a narrow-breadth uptrend: 55.2% of Nifty 500 stocks sit above their 50-DMA, 48.2% above their 200-DMA, and 7 of 11 sectors are healthy. In that same market, Netweb lost 26.00% over three months (-30.61% 63-day RS). Meanwhile, Stage 2 leaders like Coforge (+12.23% 1M, RS +9.22%), Zydus Lifesciences (+5.68% 1M, RS +3.67%), and Laurus Labs (+18.39% 1M, RS +25.29%) trend cleanly higher. Holding a Stage 4 laggard in an uptrend carries steep opportunity cost.

Upward-only stop ratchet and exit lines: we raise our hard weekly-close stop on all 73 Zerodha shares from ₹3,703.75 to ₹3,716.48. That matches the 25 November live TV floor and the 23 November 63-day low (₹3,716.10). A weekly close below ₹3,716.48 triggers a full exit. On bounces, ₹4,217.26 (200-day SMA) to ₹4,440.99 (50-day SMA) is our EXIT_ON_BOUNCE sell zone. New cash stays REJECTED unless Netweb builds a Stage 1 base and breaks above ₹4,556.98 on strong volume with daily RSI above 55.

web_blocks.title: Why the Tape Sniffed Out the Working-Capital Strain Early
paragraphs: On 12 November, Netweb's chart dip looked like a routine valuation cooldown after +335.7% Q2 sales growth. Our Pass 1 audit shows why funds stayed away even after a 31% drop. Investors are pricing in ₹766.7 crore of 40-day QIP cash burn, ₹23.8 crore quarterly finance costs, an implied 13.3% H2 sales step-down, and the February 2027 lock-up expiry.

When cash-flow forensics and Stage 4 charts both flash red, respect the tape. Do not average down below a broken 200-day average. Raise your stop and use relief bounces to rotate into Stage 2 leaders.

book_paragraphs: Let us read the tape with complete honesty, because in a high-beta hardware cycle the chart is not a decorative appendix — it is your early-warning radar. Every figure in this chapter is cleanly dated to its exact source: the verified 23 November 2026 NSE market-facts ledger (where Netweb closed at ₹4,010.60, down 2.07% on the day) and the live 25 November 2026 TradingView snapshot (where Netweb closed at ₹4,010.80, flat on the session). Across both feeds, the technical picture has deteriorated materially since our 12 November review.

Back on 12 November 2026, Netweb traded at ₹4,151.90 — clinging within 0.65% of its 200-day simple moving average, with a flickering 4-hour bounce that offered hope of stabilisation. Over the next two weeks, that hope evaporated. As of 25 November 2026, Netweb has decisively broken its 200-day average (₹4,217.26) and sits 4.90% below it. It is 9.69% below a falling 50-day average (₹4,440.99), 11.99% below its 30-week average (₹4,556.98), and 6.64% below its 10-week exponential average (₹4,296.24). In Stan Weinstein's framework, sustained trade below a declining 30-week average is Stage 4 — the declining phase. The deterministic timing gate reads CAP_REJECTED, and Netweb is absent from TheWrap Stage 2 list.

Look down to the 4-hour chart and the momentum oscillators, and you will see why there is not even a tactical swing trade here. Daily RSI sits at 40.96 on TradingView (39.96 on the 23 November NSE ledger), weekly RSI is 43.49, and 4-hour RSI has rolled back down to 42.50. Price at ₹4,010.80 is trapped beneath both its 4-hour 20-EMA (₹4,078.19) and 4-hour 50-SMA (₹4,177.81). Notice also that Netweb is not part of the NSE F&O segment, meaning there is no liquid options chain to hedge downside or express asymmetric call convexity. Every rupee of risk must be managed directly in cash equity.

Volume and distribution tell an equally clear story. Over the past 25 trading sessions, the NSE ledger counts 8 distribution days — sessions where institutions sold into the tape on heavy volume. Meanwhile, recent sessions have traded at just 0.51x to 0.64x normal volume, showing an absence of institutional bargain hunting. Daily ATR is ₹185.30, or 4.62% of the share price, which means a routine two-day swing can wipe out ₹370 per share. Bollinger-band width has narrowed from 27.3% to 14.77%, but tightening bands below a broken 200-day average and falling 50-day average are not a bullish coil — they often precede a continuation break if the ₹3,716 swing low gives way.

We must also reconcile a technical detail between our two data feeds so nothing is swept under the rug. The 23 November NSE ledger tags Netweb as Stage 1 (Basing) because price has held above its 63-day low of ₹3,716.10. The 25 November TradingView classifier tags it as Stage 4 because price is 12% below its 30-week SMA and nearly 10% below a falling 50-day SMA. Which one governs your capital? Stage 4. A real Stage 1 base requires months of sideways absorption, a flattening 30-week average, and fading distribution. Eight distribution days in 25 sessions and -30.6% 63-day relative strength against Nifty 50 is not quiet institutional accumulation.

That relative-strength collapse is the most important context of all. Per the 23 November ledger, Nifty 50 is in a narrow-breadth uptrend with 55.2% of Nifty 500 stocks above their 50-day averages and 7 of 11 sectors healthy. In that exact same market, Stage 2 Indian holdings like Coforge, Zydus Lifesciences, and Laurus Labs are trending higher above rising averages, while Netweb has shed 26% over three months and lagged the benchmark by more than 30 percentage points. Institutional money is voting with its feet, rotating out of working-capital-intensive hardware into cleaner earnings compounders.

Shareholding structure explains the overhead supply that will cap near-term rallies. Promoter ownership dropped from 75.45% at IPO to 64.16% by September 2026, including a ₹514+ crore block sale of 3.65% by four promoters in February 2026 whose 12-month no-dilution commitment expires in February 2027. Foreign institutional investors have trimmed from above 12% to 9.47%, retail shareholder count has ballooned past 2.6 lakh, and August 2026 QIP funds who bought at ₹4,790 are sitting 16.3% underwater. Every rally back toward ₹4,217–₹4,441 — and certainly toward ₹4,557–₹4,790 — will run straight into trapped holders eager to break even.

That brings us to our exact price discipline. Under our upward-only stop-loss ratchet rule, we raise the hard weekly-close stop on our 73 held Zerodha shares from ₹3,703.75 to ₹3,716.48 — matching the live 25 November TradingView invalidation floor and the 23 November 63-day swing low of ₹3,716.10. If ₹3,716.48 breaks on a weekly close, we exit all 73 shares immediately. If the stock instead stages a relief rally into the broken 200-day SMA (₹4,217.26) through the falling 50-day SMA (₹4,440.99), we treat that strength as an exit gift, not a buy signal. And for new capital, the tape joins valuation and cash flow in delivering a clear verdict: stay out until a genuine Stage 1 base and a high-volume Stage 2 breakout above ₹4,556.98 prove the selling is over.

book_callouts.title: The Broken 200-Day Shelf
book_callouts.text: On 12 November, Netweb was still clinging to its 200-day SMA (-0.65%). By 25 November, it has broken 4.90% below the 200-day SMA (₹4,217.26), logged 8 distribution days in 25 sessions, and lost its 4-hour bounce turn. The ratcheted ₹3,716.48 weekly-close stop is the last line of defence; any bounce into ₹4,217–₹4,441 is overhead supply to exit into, not a new-money entry.
